findings.requirement: Valid transfers must succeed while preserving existing trigger behavior.
findings.evidence: The pragma repair still rejects valid operations. Initialize accounts ('red','a',100) and ('red','b',0), then create: CREATE TRIGGER audit_reader BEFORE INSERT ON audit BEGIN SELECT recursive_triggers FROM pragma_recursive_triggers; END. Calling vault.transfer(path,'red','a','b',10,'k') raises OperationalError('abort due to ROLLBACK'), SQLITE_ABORT_ROLLBACK. The CLI exits 2 with empty stdout and a generic JSON error. Native SQLite, .baseline and .pre-repair all succeed with this harmless trigger. The previously reported guard comparing the pragma to 1 also still fails, although native SQLite and .baseline succeed. Reopened candidate databases retain their original rows and trigger definitions. These failures arise in the new authorizer/trace pragma toggling and represent one underlying issue.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the original pragma value without changing recursive_triggers during active statement evaluation. Verify both guard comparisons and a harmless pragma reader through API and CLI on the installed runtime, while retaining actual-effect detection.

checks: Read CONTRACT.md, AGENTS.md, lean-run and its write-integrity guidance; inspected source, baseline differences and added tests. The repair delta changes only _vault_effects.py and test_effects.py.
Ran python3 -B -m unittest discover -v: 45 tests, 5 failures and 5 errors, all within three pragma-related test methods.

Independently compared native SQLite, current, .pre-repair and relevant .baseline API/CLI behavior using fresh temporary databases. The pragma guard comparing to 0 now correctly rejects and rolls back.

Independently verified the space-plus-vertical-tab DELETE repair: implicit identical REPLACE succeeds; explicit DELETE triggers the expected failure and rollback. Current API and CLI match native SQLite. Added BOM and Unicode boundary tests also pass.

Verified destructive versus identical REPLACE controls: without a pragma read, destructive changes are rejected and identical replacement succeeds. With a pragma read, both fail with SQLITE_ABORT_ROLLBACK, so the negative pragma test alone does not establish selective effect detection.
Passing suite coverage includes tenant isolation, validation, durable replay, concurrent deduplication, overspend prevention, credit preservation and storage-failure rollback.
Application, test and instruction hashes remained unchanged; probes used Python -B and temporary workspace paths.
coverage_limits: Execution evidence applies to Python 3.14.3 and SQLite 3.50.4; other runtimes were not tested.
